q: 1. The shades and shadows are :
options: the result of object on the ground
the result of light on the ground
explain: Shades refer to the dark parts on the object itself, while shadows are the dark areas cast by the object onto another surface.

q: 2. The face of an object containing circles, irregular shapes, etc. is kept parallel to the plane of projection is known as .............
explain: In oblique projection, the face with circular or irregular details is deliberately kept parallel to the plane of projection so it can be drawn true to shape without distortion, while other faces recede at an angle.

q: 3. The base angles used for drawing an isometric projection are:
explain: Isometric drawing uses one vertical (0° from vertical) axis and two receding axes drawn at 30° to the horizontal.

q: 4. The curve of intersection of a vertical cone with an auxiliary vertical plane is .............
explain: An auxiliary vertical plane cutting a cone parallel to one of its generators (slant lines) produces a parabolic section, as per the conic section relationships.

q: 5. Select the incorrect statement about orthographic projections :
options: the reference planes are also called the principle planes
the object must the situated in the first quadrant
the planes of projection and assumed to be transparent
projections are obtained by drawing perpendicular s from the object to the planes
explain: While the planes are assumed transparent in 3rd angle, the statement is contextually marked incorrect based on general principle definitions in the key.

q: 6. In the first angle method of orthographic projection
options: the object comes between the observer and the plane
the plane comes between the object and the observer
the observer comes between the object and the plane
explain: In first-angle projection, the sequence is Observer -> Object -> Plane.

q: 7. Isometric projection is:
options: an orthographic projection of pictorial type
explain: Isometric projection is technically a form of orthographic (pictorial) projection, and is also commonly grouped among pictorial/oblique-type projections used in drafting.

q: 8. Most suitable hand drawn coloured perspective drawing paper is:
explain: Any good quality coloured paper is considered suitable for hand-drawn coloured perspective presentation drawings.

q: 9. In general structural drawings would typically include following information:
explain: Structural drawings are comprehensive and include orientation (North), geometric views, and material specifications.

q: 10. *A technical drawing of an object that shows the relationship or order of assembly of the various parts is known
explain: An exploded view drawing shows the components of an object separated but in their correct relative positions for assembly.

q: 11. In 1st angle projection the right side view must be drawn on .... side of the FV:
explain: In first angle projection each view is placed on the side opposite to the direction it is viewed from, so the right side view appears to the left of the front view.

q: 12. When the receding lines are drawn to full size scale then the oblique projection is
explain: In Cavalier projection, the receding (depth) axis is drawn at its full actual length.

q: 13. Perspective drawing are mostly used in drawing:
options: elevation of proposed building, exhibition stalls bridges etc.
side view of proposed building, exhibition stalls bridges etc.
explain: As given by the answer key, none of the specific listed options is the standard answer; perspective drawings are generally used for realistic presentation views rather than technical plans/elevations.

q: 14. When the receding lines are drawn to half size scale then the oblique projection is
explain: In Cabinet projection, the receding axis is reduced by half to create a more realistic appearance to the human eye.

q: 15. The angle that isometric lines make with each other is .............
explain: The isometric lines (edges parallel to the isometric axes) are mutually inclined at 120° to each other, giving the standard isometric drawing its symmetric triangular appearance.

q: 16. A square in a regular multi-view projection appears in an isometric view as .............
explain: A square face, when drawn in isometric view (inclined to the viewer along isometric axes), is foreshortened into a rhombus shape.

q: 17. The illusion of depth in paintings is depicting by .............
explain: Aerial (atmospheric) perspective creates the illusion of depth in paintings through variations in color, tone, and clarity (distant objects appearing hazier/lighter), as distinct from linear (vanishing-point) perspective methods.

q: 18. The number of stages that are necessary to get the orthographic views of a solid having its axis inclined to both the reference planes .............
explain: When a solid's axis is inclined to both HP and VP, obtaining its true orthographic views requires a sequence of three stages: drawing it in simple position, tilting the axis to the given inclination with one plane, then further changing position relative to the other plane.

q: 19. A tetrahedron is resting on its face on the HP with a side perpendicular to the VP. Its front view will be .............
explain: With a tetrahedron resting on a triangular face on HP and one edge perpendicular to VP, the front view (projected along the direction perpendicular to VP) appears as an isosceles triangle due to the way the base edge foreshortens.

q: 20. A square pyramid is resting on a face in the VP. The number of dotted lines that will appear in the front view .............
explain: With the square pyramid resting on a triangular face against VP, the hidden (invisible) edges behind the visible face project as two dotted (hidden) lines in the front view.

q: 21. The elevation is a:
explain: An elevation can refer to the front, back, or side view of an object depending on which vertical face is being projected.

q: 22. The method by which the development of surface of an oblique solid is obtained .............
explain: Since an oblique solid's surface lacks the regular symmetry needed for exact radial-line or parallel-line development, its development is obtained approximately, using the approximation method.

q: 23. Methods for the development of solids are .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'triangular method' is marked as the sole correct answer, though in general practice, parallel-line, radial-line, and triangulation methods are all standard techniques for surface development of solids.

q: 24. Isometric drawing fall into a larger category of drawings known as .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'perspective drawings' is marked correct; conventionally isometric drawings fall under the broader category of pictorial (or axonometric) drawings rather than perspective drawings, but the given key selects option (d).

q: 25. If a thin rectangular plate of 60 mm × 30 mm is inclined at an angle of 60° to HP its top view may be .............
explain: When the 60 mm side (perpendicular to VP) is inclined at 60° to HP, its projected length in the top view foreshortens to approximately 30 mm (60×cos60°=30), making the top view a square of 30 mm side (30×30).

q: 26. In multi-view orthographic projection, the front view of a circular plane may be .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'an ellipse' is marked correct here; conventionally, depending on the plane's orientation, the front view of a circular plane can be a circle, ellipse, or straight line, so 'any one of these' would be the general case, but the given key selects option (b) for this specific item.

q: 27. If both front and top views of a plane are straight lines the true shape will lie on .............
explain: When both principal views collapse to straight lines, the plane is perpendicular to both HP and VP, meaning it is parallel to the profile plane; conventionally this would place the true shape on the profile plane specifically, but per this reference, option (d) is marked as the general answer.

q: 28. If a circular plane is inclined at 30° with the HP and 60° with the VP its side view will be .............
explain: Since the given inclinations (30° to HP and 60° to VP) sum to 90°, the plane is perpendicular to the profile plane, so its side view is seen edge-on as a straight line.

q: 29. Picture plane is
explain: The picture plane, on which the perspective image is formed, is taken as a vertical plane.

q: 30. In the case of orthographic projection the number of view used are
explain: The complete orthographic (glass-box) system generally uses six principal views.

q: 31. A circle is in isometric projection appears as
explain: Due to the inclination of isometric faces to the line of sight, a circle is foreshortened and appears as an ellipse.

q: 32. Oblique projections are of .............
explain: Oblique projections (cavalier and cabinet types) commonly use receding lines drawn at either 30° or 45° to the horizontal, so both angles are used depending on the projection type.

q: 33. In isometric projection the receding lines are drawn with horizontal at
explain: The receding isometric axes are conventionally drawn at 30° to the horizontal.

q: 34. Development of sphere is done by .............
options: parallel line or radial line method
explain: Since a sphere's doubly curved surface cannot be developed exactly, it is approximately developed using the zone (band) method or the lune (gore) method, both specialized techniques for spherical surfaces.

q: 35. When a bullet is shot in air the path traversed by the bullet is called .............
explain: Under gravity and ignoring air resistance, a projectile such as a bullet follows a parabolic trajectory through the air.

q: 36. Isometric drawings fall into the category of .............
explain: Isometric drawing is one specific type within the broader category of axonometric drawings, which are orthographic projections with the object rotated to reveal multiple faces.

q: 37. The projectors in isometric view are .............
explain: Isometric projection is a form of orthographic (parallel) projection, so its projectors remain parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 38. The way of illustrating three dimensional objects in a two dimensional drawing is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'perspective' is marked correct here; more broadly, several methods (axonometric, perspective, oblique) are used to represent 3D objects in 2D, but the given key highlights perspective as the intended answer for this item.

q: 39. When primarily information is drawn in elevation, the interpretation is done by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'cavalier projection' is marked correct; cavalier oblique projection retains true (full) scale along the receding axis, which supports interpretation when the front (elevation) face carries the primary information.

q: 40. A cone resting on its base in the HP is penetrated by a horizontal cylinder. The top view of the curve of intersection results in .............
explain: When a horizontal cylinder fully penetrates a cone resting on its base, the resulting intersection curve, seen in the top view, forms a closed loop as the cylinder passes through both sides of the cone's surface.

q: 41. The curve of intersection of a vertical cylinder with an auxiliary vertical plane is .............
explain: An auxiliary vertical plane cutting through a vertical cylinder (parallel to its axis) produces a rectangular section, so the curve of intersection along the cylindrical surface appears as a straight line (generator).

q: 42. The ratio of isometric length and true length of the object is .............
explain: The isometric scale ratio, commonly cited as approximately 0.816 in most texts, is represented here (per the answer key) as 0.58, reflecting a specific numerical value used in this reference.

q: 43. The projection of any feature on the horizontal plane is called .............
explain: The projection of any object or feature onto the horizontal plane (viewed from above) is termed the plan (or top view).

q: 44. The line joining any point on the object to the station point is known as .............
explain: In perspective drawing, the imaginary line connecting a point on the object to the observer's eye (station point) is called a visual ray (or line of sight).

q: 45. Pictorial views are obtained by .............
explain: Isometric, oblique, and perspective projections are all classified as pictorial projection methods, each producing a three-dimensional-looking view of the object in a single drawing.

q: 46. In an oblique projection, the front surface of the object is kept at an angle with respect to plane of projection is .............
explain: In oblique projection, the front (principal) face of the object is deliberately kept parallel to the plane of projection so it appears true to shape, while the receding lines are drawn at an angle.

q: 47. A solid having minimum number of faces is .............
explain: A tetrahedron has only 4 triangular faces, the minimum possible number of flat faces for any closed 3D polyhedron, fewer than a triangular prism (5), square pyramid (5), or cube (6).

q: 48. When a pendulum oscillates, name the locus of a point moving along its string at a constant speed .............
explain: A point moving at constant speed along a pendulum's string, whose length itself changes (winds/unwinds) uniformly, traces a spiral curve.

q: 49. What type of views is used to provide clarity and reveal interior features of a part?
explain: Section views are created by imagining the object cut along a plane, exposing interior details that would otherwise be hidden, thereby improving clarity of internal features.

q: 50. A cone is cut by a section plane parallel to the profile plane. Its true shape of section is seen in .............
explain: Since the cutting plane is parallel to the profile plane, the true shape of the resulting section is revealed in the side (profile) view, which is taken looking along a direction parallel to that plane.
